reading.body:
All three digital forensics openings here are federal government roles, two at the Postal Service and one at the DEA, with no AI company hiring in the set.

The three postings were collected from USAJobs and posted between August 27 and September 14, 2026. Pay bands run from $78,160 to $187,093. Two are Postal Service forensic computer analyst positions, one in Cleveland, Ohio and a senior one in Richmond, California. The third is a Drug Enforcement Administration supervisory chemist for forensic instruction in Quantico, Virginia, which is a laboratory and teaching job rather than a computer job, so the category label covers more than the titles suggest.

What this measures is government capacity to examine digital evidence, which scales with the volume of digital records and digital crime rather than with model training. Nothing in these records connects to compute, data centers, or power, and the employers are public agencies, so the pay bands say nothing about what AI labs pay for comparable technical work.

Three records cannot describe a market. The source list includes aggregators, remote job boards, and European listings, but every posting in this set came from USAJobs, so private-sector and non-US demand is absent. There is no time series here, so no direction of travel can be read from it.
